question: What is the minimum annual contribution (in Rs.) required to open and maintain an NPS Vatsalya account launched in September 20247
solution:
The correct answer is __**1000**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__

• The **NPS Vatsalya account**, introduced in **September 2024**, is a new initiative under the National Pension Scheme (NPS) aimed at providing financial security.

• The minimum annual contribution required to open and maintain this account is **Rs. 1000**, making it accessible for a broad segment of the population.

• This initiative is particularly tailored to encourage savings for retirement and financial protection for individuals.

• The NPS Vatsalya account follows the broader framework of the NPS, emphasizing tax benefits and flexible investment options.

• Contributors can build a retirement corpus over time with relatively low annual contributions, ensuring inclusivity and financial planning for individuals across different income groups.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__

• **About NPS:**

• The **National Pension Scheme (NPS)** is a government-sponsored pension scheme launched in **2004** for government employees and extended to all citizens in **2009**.

• It aims to provide financial security in old age through regular contributions over an individual’s working life.

• Investors can choose between various asset classes, such as equities, corporate bonds, and government securities, for their contributions.

• Subscribers receive a regular pension after retirement, based on the corpus accumulated during their working years.

• **Features of NPS Vatsalya:**

• The **NPS Vatsalya account** has been introduced to expand the reach of the NPS scheme and encourage savings among lower-income groups.

• It requires a **minimum annual contribution of Rs. 1000**, which is affordable for most individuals.

• The scheme offers **tax benefits** under Section 80C and Section 80CCD of the Income Tax Act, 1961.

• Flexibility in contributions allows subscribers to save and grow their retirement corpus according to their financial capacity.

• **Benefits of the NPS:**

• Subscribers receive a **fixed monthly pension** after retirement, depending on the accumulated savings.

• Investments under NPS are managed by professional fund managers, ensuring optimal returns for subscribers.

• Partial withdrawals are permitted under specific conditions, such as education, marriage, or critical illness.

• **Eligibility for NPS Vatsalya Account:**

• Any Indian citizen between the **ages of 18 and 65** can open an NPS Vatsalya account.

• The scheme is designed to promote financial inclusion among individuals in both urban and rural areas.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

• **Comparison of Contribution Limits:**

• The **minimum annual contribution** for an NPS Vatsalya account is **Rs. 1000**, which is lower than the typical minimum contribution required for regular NPS accounts.

• There is **no upper limit** for contributions, allowing individuals to save more based on their financial goals.

• **Tax Benefits:**

• Contributions to the NPS are eligible for tax deductions of up to **Rs. 1.5 lakh** under Section 80C of the Income Tax Act.

• Additional deductions of up to **Rs. 50,000** are available under Section 80CCD(1B), making it an attractive savings tool.

• **Withdrawal Rules:**

• Subscribers can withdraw up to **25%** of their contributions after completing three years in the scheme, for specific purposes such as higher education or medical emergencies.

• At retirement, subscribers must use at least **40%** of their corpus to purchase an annuity, ensuring a steady income post-retirement.

• **Role of PFRDA:**

• The **Pension Fund Regulatory and Development Authority (PFRDA)** regulates the NPS and ensures its smooth functioning.

• The PFRDA also approves and monitors fund managers responsible for managing subscribers’ investments.
